item: W7 selection-rule sweep over the banked W7-FULL windows
_class: EXPLORATORY (re-uses the W7 scoring windows; a winning rule must be re-measured on a fresh grid)
read: The roll-consistency cost's argmin sits at error-rank 132 of 256 - the MEDIAN, i.e. no better than chance at the extreme - and the mean error inside its top-m is flat at ~5.32 for every m, the fan's own mean. The cost does not identify good candidates over the full fan on the repaired trunk; W7's deployed 3.3348 comes from the KINEMATIC term (weight 0.2), not from roll consistency. The top-m CEILINGS do fall (0.356 at m=32), so a better rule inside a top-m set is possible - but not by argmin.
actionable: w7_roll_rerank's anti-degeneracy PROGRESS term (--w-prog, 'MINUS candidate arc length') has been weight 0.0 in EVERY W7 run to date. A roll-consistency cost is trivially minimised by a degenerate near-stationary candidate, which is exactly the failure shape; enabling and sweeping w_prog is the first cheap test.
